<violet-conversation-thread style="block-size: 400px; border: 1px solid rgba(28, 26, 13, 0.1); border-radius: 8px;"><violet-message message-role="user" tone="default"><violet-message-text state="done">Tell me about composting.</violet-message-text></violet-message><violet-message message-role="assistant" tone="default"><violet-message-text state="done">Composting is the natural process of recycling organic matter into a valuable fertilizer. You can compost fruit scraps, vegetable peels, coffee grounds, eggshells, yard trimmings, and more.</violet-message-text></violet-message><violet-message message-role="user" tone="default"><violet-message-text state="done">How do I get started?</violet-message-text></violet-message><violet-message message-role="assistant" tone="default"><violet-message-text state="done">Start with a bin or designated area. Layer green materials (food scraps, fresh grass) with brown materials (dried leaves, cardboard). Keep it moist and turn it regularly.</violet-message-text></violet-message><violet-message message-role="user" tone="default"><violet-message-text state="done">How long does it take?</violet-message-text></violet-message><violet-message message-role="assistant" tone="default"><violet-message-text state="done">Hot composting can produce usable compost in 4-8 weeks with regular turning. Cold composting takes 6-12 months but requires less effort.</violet-message-text></violet-message><violet-message message-role="user" tone="default"><violet-message-text state="done">What should I avoid adding?</violet-message-text></violet-message><violet-message message-role="assistant" tone="default"><violet-message-text state="done">Avoid meat, dairy, oils, diseased plants, pet waste, and treated wood. These can attract pests, create odors, or introduce harmful substances.</violet-message-text></violet-message><violet-message message-role="user" tone="default"><violet-message-text state="done">Can I compost in an apartment?</violet-message-text></violet-message><violet-message message-role="assistant" tone="default"><violet-message-text state="done">Yes! Vermicomposting (worm composting) works great indoors. A small worm bin under the sink can process kitchen scraps quietly and without odor when maintained properly.</violet-message-text></violet-message></violet-conversation-thread>
